item.title: [Zhang Xiaojun Podcast] 147. 和蚂蚁灵波沈宇军聊：机器人原生基础模型、大脑和本体的关系、预训练与数据scale up、老师汤晓鸥
item.dc:creator: Zhang Xiaojun Podcast
item.content:encoded:
💡 创造性洞见

一、最反直觉的观察：中国机器人生态正在"角色互换"

过去十年的产业刻板印象是——美国团队做大脑，中国团队做本体。但 2026 年出现的这波"从本体转向大脑"的浪潮，实际上是中国硬件太成熟带来的反噬。当灵巧手从"稀缺"走向"即将标准化"，当传感器从算力受限走向富余，整条硬件价值链正在快速下沉为"大宗商品"。价值必然向上游迁移——这不是因为大家突然爱上了大脑，而是硬件红利到期后的资本自然选择。沈宇军讲的"下一代硬件会由智能重新定义"其实是同一句话的镜像表达：现在做本体的人在为下一代模型公司提供过渡形态。

一个更有意思的镜像：美国 PI 押注 zero-shot（尽量不做后训练），而中国的灵波、Generalist 强调"高效后训练"——这看似技术路线之争，深层其实是基础设施可用性差异塑造出来的哲学：数据丰沛地区可以赌通用，数据稀缺地区不得不押可迁移性。技术路线在多大程度上是环境的映射，比研究者自己愿意承认的要多得多。

二、"玻璃门后的猫"是一次隐秘的哲学声明

沈宇军举的那个例子——数字世界的 DINO 能穿透玻璃"看见"猫，但物理世界必须先看到玻璃、后看到猫——听起来只是一个技术差异，实际上暴露了过去十年的视觉大模型是"作弊长大的"：bidirectional attention 让模型学会了 X 光透视，因为损失函数从不惩罚"透过遮挡看东西"。这类模型进入机器人时的失败，本质上是认识论的失败：它们理解的是"存在性"（有一只猫），机器人需要的是"可达性"（能不能碰到）。

这一点可以直接连到康德——digital world 学到的是"物自体"，physical world 学到的是"现象"。有趣的是，机器学习领域实际上是反过来的：数字模型学"表象"，反而绕过了物理约束；物理模型才不得不面对现象学式的"遮挡、时序、单向"。灵波从零训练一套单向 attention + MOE 的架构，等于是在给机器人重造一整套"可用的经验主义感官系统"。

三、MOE 训练失败几十次的另一种读法：组织行为学

沈宇军说"MOE 是能力问题不是态度问题"——训练要保证每个专家被均匀激活，否则就退化成小 dense 模型。这几乎是组织管理的隐喻在数学层面上的显现：如果没有强力的均衡机制，任何"专家网络"都会自然演化出少数明星承担所有工作、多数人被闲置的形态。这不是懒惰，这是梯度下降在寻找最短路径，就像组织里的人自然会把活推给最能干的那个。

MOE 需要显式的 balance loss + 采样策略 + 惩罚项才能稳定训练，其实等于说：任何多元协作系统都需要制度性均衡设计，否则最终结果就是"表面上是团队、本质上是独裁"。这个洞察从数学一路穿到管理学、政治学、乃至生态学（顶级捕食者垄断能量流）。

四、最容易被忽视的战略动作：先把"双向"改成"单向"再重训 pre-train

绝大多数团队在做机器人的时候会想着"复用现成的视频生成大模型"，因为那省事。灵波却选择从头训一个单向 attention 的原生视觉压缩器。这看起来是浪费——但它揭示了一个通用原理：当下游任务的物理约束与上游模型的假设根本矛盾时，"改造"永远比"重建"更贵。数字世界的 pretrained knowledge 存在双向注意力里，强行改成单向就会大规模遗忘——就像你不能通过"删除左脑"把一个双语者变成单语者。

这个模式在其他领域也惊人地反复出现：Tesla 不用激光雷达是同款决策（不复用其他自动驾驶栈的成果，从纯视觉重训）；Apple 造 M 系列芯片是同款决策（不 patch x86，从 ARM 重建）。凡是敢在关键抽象层做"从零开始"的公司，事后回看都拿到了架构级红利。灵波在这一次押注中，赌的是"数据原生"会成为下一个类似的分水岭——比模型架构原生更根本，因为它决定了未来十年谁能真正 scale。

五、隐藏的悖论：他们做的是"大脑"，但真正的核心是"感官"

整场访谈最反直觉的一点是——沈宇军讲"做大脑"，但他反复强调的技术选择全是关于感官系统的：从传感器开始学、深度模型是视觉基础、Varian 强调对空间的多层次理解、触觉传感器要重新定义指标。这暗示了一个尚未被产业充分讨论的判断：通用机器人时代的"智能"瓶颈可能不在推理，而在感知。LLM 已经证明了"如果输入信号足够干净，reasoning 会自发涌现"。所以真正稀缺的是给机器人一副能匹配任务的眼睛、皮肤、和时间感。

这从生物学得到印证：动物界智能的爆发从来不是先长脑子再造眼睛，而是寒武纪大爆发时视觉先出现，然后脑容量才随之扩张。灵波的路径其实是在重演这段自然史。这也解释了他为什么说"我们不做本体但会重新定义传感器指标"——下一波机器人的分水岭很可能不在模型规模，而在感官保真度与任务对齐度。

📝 转录文本

开场引言

Hello everyone, I'm Xiaojun. In the year of 2026, a new phenomenon emerged in the Chinese technology industry. A group of companies that started from the robot brain are now focusing on the body. This phenomenon is counterintuitive, because in the past, people thought that the Vigo robot team was more focused on brain research, while the Chinese robot team was more focused on hardware and the body.

In our last episode, I interviewed a researcher from PIE, Physical Intelligence. This is a laboratory in Guigu that is under the spotlight for robot brains. The industry is comparing them to the OpenAI of robots. Today I invite a company that is exploring the origin of the giant model of the original body in the local area. It is a subsidiary of Ant Group, Ant灵波. Currently, the second generation of giant basic models has just been released. I talked to its chief scientist Shen Yujun.

How to start from the prehistoric age to a robot's base? What is the bottleneck? Where is the GPT-1 moment of the robot? You can also feel some fusion and difference between Chinese and American ideas. Next, I will interview Shen Yujun. Looking forward to our joint progress in AI in 2026.

"我还是相信 G-SEN 一定会有自己的模型。如果这个观点不变，它的数据一定要支撑它做出自己的模型。如何 scale up 数据是至关重要的一点。" "从目前行业来看，大脑很可能是滞后于本体的。" "如果机器人有人格，你希望它是什么人格？我希望它是 J 人。好干活。它的核心还是要实用。"

一、沈宇军的背景：从商汤到自研，再到 AI 迁徙

Hello, let's say hello to the audience first.

Hello, I'm Shen Yujun. I'm currently working as a chief scientist at Ants and Ants Technology.

你之前在清华，然后来了港中文。跟我们聊聊你在 AI 领域的一系列探索。

It's also a coincidence. When I was studying in Tsinghua, I happened to be in the third year of college. At that time, ShangTang was just established — end of 2014. Our third year required an internship for the first semester. At that time, ShangTang was just in the middle of… I was a bit confused when I went there. Although AI was popular, I didn't know what I liked to do. So I tried many different directions.

I was good at testing and sorting. They won many championships. But I wasn't interested in numbering. I chose to do this next — I wanted to do it in the direction of life model. I started doing life model in 2017. I was working on a series of popular projects, especially the StyleGAN series.

Then I wanted to see if I could make it better. I mean, from editing to making it better. Now, people would say it's called pre-training. At that time, there was no such concept. To put it bluntly, I wanted to train the life model. But after training, I found that this thing was completely different. I was not able to control myself. I didn't have the right to say anything about the output. I didn't know how to make the model better. I started to think about moving forward.

二、GAN 到 Diffusion 的转折

你什么时候发现 GAN 无法 scale？

This is a very interesting story. Even this year, I was still trying to do it this year. It's still not dead yet. Yes, even after Diffusion became popular, and people started to do some production with self-return, even then, our team still insisted on doing scale-up for a while.

How to say — it actually achieved a certain effect. A while ago, we made a GAN model and released it. At that time, I found that it was not as good as Diffusion in some aspects. But it is still much better than previous technology. It has its value.

But the biggest problem is that the efficiency of the computing is too low. Because Diffusion can be used many times and generate a map. We think that it is very complicated to generate content, especially when you want to generate videos. Because there is too much content in it. Then it may not be the best way to do it.

But to go back to what I said, I think GAN is a way to fight against the internet. The core technology is still fighting against it. If you want to train two models at the same time, and let them interact with each other, and fight each other, we have accumulated something in this regard. This technology itself, if we leave GAN alone…

三、从学界到工业界：字节、蚂蚁与自我怀疑

The content of the presentation was not yet in the scope of the business of ShangTang. Actually, when I graduated, I joined ByteDance. It was very similar to what I did — because they did Douyin, Douyin was originally content, and they needed a lot of special effects.

I remember at that time, I did some work during my studies. At that time, I also brought some interesting applications, because I was doing image editing. Then just see if I can pass some AI technology. For example, let your boy become a girl. Then get old, get younger. Just look at some — there should be some playlists at that time. For example, look at what you should look like 20 years later. What should you look like when you're 70?

这像是在做 computer vision。

Yes, it's a good summary. It's like doing computer vision. To be honest, I think the first wave of computer vision in the past decade is face recognition. This is a big application. The second wave is Tesla's fire — it has launched a pure visual solution. Apart from that, there is no visual application that is used on a large scale and has a relatively strong industrial value. It seems that it has not yet encountered such a specific scene. This is why I originally wanted to switch from visual to…

At that time, in 2024, I started to do this.

四、蚂蚁的路径：从数字世界走向物理世界

I think the most popular one is about finance. But ants have done a lot of things like healthcare, travel, and so on. Ants have done a lot of things related to digital world and life services. And then, from the perspective of the whole group, if the services of the digital world are to be extended further, they will definitely be moved to the physical world. And then, at the end of 2024, ants officially announced that they would establish a company.

蚂蚁研究院有多大？

If we still treat it as a research institution, it is very likely to be out of the industry. Or in other words, the advanced technology that researchers think and the advanced technology needed by the industry will have a gap. So I think this is actually a relatively wise choice. That is, since we want to do it, we will turn it into a real business. Instead of turning it into a research-oriented test team. So we established such a company.

You have experienced three groups, including the ant research department and the ant灵波 department: - The first is a product company — you have to use AI technology to supply it. - The second is a research drive. - The third is a business-based company, similar to a startup.

From the first time I saw a large model to the explosion of a large model, I was also hit by a wave. At that time, I was a little confused. What kind of research is good? If you send a paper or get more money, does it mean you are very successful? When I was younger, I was interested in the academic circle. When I grew up, I was interested in the industry. What does it bring? Is this research valuable?

Then I came to the current 具身 industry. This time, I actually feel deeper. I think it is a combination of the two. That is, we both want to do something different. I don't want to pick a completely new one. I want to pick a more solid one. I think from this perspective, I think 具身 is a better choice.

五、加入灵波：naive 的一课

你刚开始的感受是什么？

Two points. The first point is that I feel too naive. I was so naive because in the year of 2024, I proposed to be a robot in the research institute. But then I realized that it was completely different from what I had imagined. There were too many things that I didn't understand about the robot track. I might have understood a little about vision and models, but how to deploy a model on a robot, how to adjust the communication inside, I feel like there are too many technical battles that are beyond my level.

The second feeling is also… how to say it? In the process, when the Limbo was first established, the whole team was less than 10 people. And then, little by little, the team was constantly growing. In the process, I felt like I was learning and changing with the industry. It was quite amazing. I think I was more aware of these two things.

六、做透明大脑的选择：不做本体

为什么不自己做本体？

We still want to be the brain of robots. This is what we have already clarified. Why not do it yourself? We hope to… Let's talk about our original intention. Because we started out with the idea of the Ma's Group's general meeting. And then we added the promotion of its life services. We still hope that one day, every family will have a robot. But nobody knows what this robot looks like. It's not certain if it's from the same brand. Just like our phones are all over the place.

But we hope that every family can have a robot. We hope that everyone in this robot or using the brain of Lin Bo. This was a big decision we made at that time.

Just like everyone uses mobile phones now, mobile phones are not a fixed brand. For example, everyone uses Apple or Huawei. There is no such statement. So, when there is no clear answer…

其实它的好处就像我刚刚说因为行业技术还不收敛，所以说它有一些一定是要有 research 的成分的，就换句话说我们要不断的去探索说智能的上限在哪里，但这个探索的本身其实就是一种 research。

But at the same time, since we are established, we will operate in the form of a company. We don't want to let research go to waste. We still hope that this can have a very strong combination with the industry. So it's like we are basically holding two hands now. One hand wants to see where the smart top line is, and the other hand is holding the ground. That is to say, this thing must be put in a real place.

七、2025 年的两个大决策：从视频学习、从传感器出发

You started in 2024 and did that every year. Yes, when it was established at the end of 2024, the first step was to figure out what we were going to do, who we were, and what we were going to do. This was a key point.

In fact, I think we made a bold decision throughout the year of 2025. It was in March of 2025 that we realized that robots may not simply be It's a thing that is too understandable. Because it has to move — it interacts with the environment. At that time, I actually began to realize that dynamic modeling, or this kind of modeling for the time being, may be an extremely important thing for the development of robots in the future.

At that time, there was no so-called WAM technology line — the world motion model. At that time, we didn't have this concept. But at that time, we firmly felt that robots must learn from videos. And learning from the video is not about taking the video for real or watching it as an image. It's really about letting him learn what he lost.

At that time, we made such a bold decision in the early 25th year. So we spent basically nine months. And then in the early 26th year, we were also relatively early at that time.

At that time, I realized a very important problem. Many times, the original intention of the development of the digital world and the needs of the physical world are not very compatible. But at that time, you can't force them to change. Because the digital world has its own logic, and they have their own application scenarios.

For example, from the perspective of video production, it hopes that the production quality is particularly high. This is the demand of the digital world. But in fact, the physical world, if you look at the robot's movements, this is not that important. But you can't push it to change the model in the opposite direction. Because they have their own rhythm.

So in 2026, this year, or half a year, we made a big decision. Since we can't push them to change, we will do it all again based on the demand of the physical world.

从头训？一点都没用大约模型？

对，从头来训。

We were determined to start from sensors, from real sensors, to solve the problem of the physical world. Because this happened when I first came to Lingbo in the end of 2024. I was too naive at that time. I thought it was very easy to move this matter to the robot. At that time, we actually tried. When I first came here, I tried to use a lot of mathematical algorithms or some models of computer vision developed before. I used them directly in the robot. Then I found that landing was completely different from what I had imagined before.

Because I did a lot of research before. In fact, there is a bad point in the academic world. It can't be called bad. Or there is a point that everyone has a bad reputation. That is, the data level is relatively clean.

This is a natural thing to do with the data you can get. So based on this, we have been insisting for 25 years that we may have to start from the sensor's dimension. The sensor's dimension includes vision and also touch. This is probably the whole of the whole of the… there are two major technical claims. One is that we may have to start from the sensor. We will do more, or it is better to understand it as space intelligence. The other major claim is that we may have to insist on learning from video — to learn from the way the physical world was born.

八、炒菜 demo 与坚定做"大脑"

2015 年 9 月你们做了一个炒菜 demo，跟你的技术路线有关吗？

The fried dish was a long-term task. We tried to solve the problem of software development. This also led us to 更加坚定地说我们一定要把大脑这个事情做实。

因为如果没有一个比较好用的大脑的话, 其实比如说, last time we were cooking, right? If we want to expand the scene, the cost of re-organizing is too high. So after that time, we may be more determined to do the brain thing well.

有两种公司、两种想法：一种是软硬一体、集成后一起往前走；一种是不做硬件、只做大脑。你选了第二种，为什么？

Our original intention is to make a transparent brain. So it's all because we have a judgment that the robot in this industry or its future may be in the family, but there may be some 逃避 in the middle. We think it's hard to say that there is a robot that really suits all tasks. Even if you are in a family, you may have different needs for this robot. Maybe from the perspective of the task, it is not a universal body. It's a scene where everything is solved. I think this thing itself may not be realized in the short term.

So in this respect, we still say that since our main business is to do the brain, we will start from the brain. We have always talked about a technical claim, that is, our brain has been defined from the beginning to hope it is cross-bonded, that is, to hope it is universal. This is also why we may have added different body data during the training process. We hope that our brain will experience these bodies during pre-training process, and understand their characteristics. Then, in the future, it may be said that when a certain scene really falls, it can be quickly…

I still insist that the body and the scene cannot be completely identical. What kind of body is suitable for what kind of scene? Maybe from the beginning of product definition, the body has already decided some things are suitable for it, some things are not suitable for it. Yes, everyone may talk about the common use now, but more will remain in the task and scene. But we also consider the hardware. We think the common use should be one more layer, that is, you also need to use the same body.

九、两代模型：2025 的四个模型与 2026 的第二代

这次一共六个模型。两代之间做了什么改变？

Actually, from what I just said, the two major decisions in 2025 and 2026 are actually more related. In 2025, we made two decisions. One is to start learning from video. The other is to do spatial intelligence — that is to say, start learning from sensors.

That's why we started in 2025 — or the four models that were launched in January this year: 1. Depth — 从传感器开始, 就是希望这个机器人对这个空间有更好的认知, 就对距离有更好的认知。 2. Video Motion Model — 从视频开始学，其实就催生了视频动作模型。 3. World Model — 说白了就是一个能让它当这个防震器，然后另一个是能让它当执行器，你可以大概这么去理解。 4. VLA — VLA 就是这个行业最主流的，然后能够真的说在场景里面去把活干好的这么一个一条技术路线吧。

这个模型训练多久？

不同模型那个开发周期不一样。像视频动作模型可能是开发最长的，基本上经历了大半年的时间。Depth 因为我们之前有一定的视觉积累，大概是三四个月。

十、第一代大脑能做什么，第二代升级了什么

The first generation of brains supported nine types of co-op. At that time, we should do some simple capture tasks. At that time, the industry did a lot of this kind of action. Some capture tasks may be solved better.

十六、MOE 训练：几十次失败

We did two more jobs in this regard. One is the video we talked about. Limbo Video itself is a model of original MOE architecture.

Actually, we may hear more about MOE. It seems that we can turn a dense into a one that doesn't need to be activated every time. For example, one of the three parameters is activated. But in fact, I really want to train MOE. It's still difficult.

Because in the training process, you have to control the proportion of the activation every time you generate. It has to be balanced. For example, you have a total of 30 parameters. And then you activate those 10 every time. There are 20 parameters that are basically not activated. This is unacceptable. Because if it is like this, it is actually the same as the 10-Bit or the 10-parameter dense model. There is no difference.

Since we want it to be abstract, you have to make it more balanced. How can we make a model — that is, the training of MOE — is to evenly activate each parameter at the same probability and then train it? This thing is actually a technical problem. It's not a degree of willingness. It's not that I want it to be less activated, so it's less activated.

The biggest part of it is MOE. MOE should be at least, just training MOE, if you want to train it, it may take two months. Otherwise, you will always find that although it is called MOE, it is a different MOE from the MOE you expected at the end.

所以我说训练 MOE 是一个能力问题, 不是一个态度问题。

你们失败了多少次？

In the middle, I failed — because it took two months, I think I failed dozens of times. But failure doesn't mean you fail after training. You will find that it is different from what you want after training. There are some parameters that are not balanced.

The biggest core of this MOE is how to activate these so-called experts with equal probability. This may involve some of the choices of loss function during training, some of the strategies of sampling, or adding some positive and negative factors to it. We added all kinds of things. Now we can guarantee that MOE can be a stable training for the technology itself.

十七、单向 attention 的抉择

Another technical point is that time cannot be rewound. We can't go back in time. We require that the entire attention is actually one-sided. Because attention, or the models that people often use in the digital world, are basically double-sided. Because it requires image quality. The more links there are, the bigger your calculation is. The bigger the calculation, the better the effect. This is for sure.

But we want to turn it into one-sided. In this place, it should be from — when it reaches 1.0, I hope to turn it into a single image. And then it took, maybe three or four months to do it. Single image training from the beginning.

It has another choice. In fact, I can say that I have a double image first. Then turn this double image into a single image. In this process, we will find that there is a big problem. Many knowledge learned in pre-training models, such as understanding of words, are actually contained in the double attention. Knowledge is contained in it. When you force it to become a single image, the single image is gone. But some of the knowledge is forgotten.

It's like doing a fee for a training. A intuitive performance of doing a fee is that you can say 100 words to him before, and he will transfer every word to you into a better video. But now you may say another 100 words to him, and only 20% or 30% of them can be transferred to a better video. The remaining 70 words he doesn't understand what he is talking about, because that knowledge has been destroyed.

So in terms of the double-sided and single-sided thing, we have made a relatively big decision. We decided to abandon the two-way and one-way route. From the very beginning, the design was one-way.

Video solved the problem of MOE. We trained MOE from the beginning. We had the ability to train MOE. Then the work of Word proved that we could also handle the one-way attention training. Then we applied all these technologies to the giant model. That is to say, the last day of the release of the model, which is VA 2.0 — a model that all the technology is combined together. It is a collection.

This machine starts from every parameter completely randomly. Then we put all the data in the machine and trained a machine model designed for giants. This is what we have been talking about in the release. The concept of giants and giants.

I remember there was a saying before that 24 years of coffee, 25 years of folding clothes, there is a new action every year. What is it this year? But I feel that this year, the demo is mentioned less. It's all about the new scene. I think it's just a short year. Then the development of software testing is also very fast.

有没有低于预期的？

Not as expected as data. Before everyone really starts to step into the giant's origin, although everyone is shouting out for data, but the real situation is that if you really don't need to make a basic model, you may not need that much data.

要多少数据？

I think it should be a million hours. I can start to say that the data of the whole model, the data of the giant and the data of the Internet may be relatively balanced. Then I can let it learn some common knowledge and learn some knowledge related to operation. I think this is an ideal state. It should start in a million hours. But before 1 million hours, I think there should be a scale of 100,000 hours. And these 100,000 hours can be used as pre-training. Pre-training is not based on digital models. It is pre-training of the giant origin.

So I think it is not as expected. Maybe it's because I didn't see the giant origin in the past year. And because there is no such thing, people's demand for data is not as strong as they thought.

二十六、机器人公司的"代际"更替

去年的机器人公司大都做本体和模型，今年明显有更多只做大脑的公司。为什么？

It feels like a two-generation robot company. Actually, I feel that a more critical point is: it's hard to use a whole body. But if you don't use it, you have to choose the right scene. It's meaningful to do it like this. It's like you designed it specifically for the scene. Because it can be designed specifically, it can be strengthened or simplified. Because the cost is what matters when it comes to landing. We can't use a whole body and do a specific task. In this case, many things will be overlapped and the cost will definitely rise.

So I think it's possible that we don't talk about the reason of the body. The first reason is that the body actually has its own threshold. Can you have the ability to produce? This is definitely a point. The second is that if the scene is not selected accurately, the design of the body must be problematic. But now, I think it's hard to decide which scene will run better. Everyone is trying.

Another point: I think from the current industry, the brain is probably behind the body at present. Brain development is behind the body. In other words, the main contradiction this year should be how to make it do its job well first.

Last year, 王兴兴 said that work is a desert. Yes, so I think we still can't do our job well. So there will be more people who want to try to solve this problem. But I think this industry, especially the brain — although the brain and the body still can't completely solve the problem — I think from the development point of view, they must be in a higher place.

Maybe the brain is behind the body now. But as more and more people come in to do the brain, maybe this road or the intelligent level will run faster. Then maybe one day it will surpass the body. At that time, it may make new needs for the body. Then the body will go again. Maybe there will be a new batch of companies that are re-defined by the intelligence at that time. It may develop in that direction.

Many things are designed to be easier to control the model. I think the body will develop for a while. Then the body will be stronger and the intelligence will be insufficient. I think it must be such a process.

前一代硬件可能不适应下一代模型？

I think so. The hardware itself may be fine. But I think the sensor should be — the current sensor should be — it needs to be further upgraded. Especially the touch sensor. For example, we have a lot of indicators for our sensor. Many times, if you only use the sensor, you will expect that the indicators are all good. But sometimes you can't really satisfy all the things, so you have to make a choice.

The previous choices may be based on the process of use. For example, the interest must be accurate. But in the age of AI, the most important thing for models is not necessarily to be accurate, but to have fast response. I may have higher practical requirements than that.

二十七、创业心得：赌与落地

2C 更 sexy。所以现在他需要做一个选择：从软件还是硬件出发？

We start from software.

下一代原生模型你怎么看？

What I just said is that we did this. From the physical characteristics, we did some original design. Then, I think the biggest thing is how to make the data origin from the structural origin, and go further and further. The data origin solves the problem of the kind of falsification we just talked about. For example, the falsification of the body structure. Then we can now do the position falsification. But then we have to do the task falsification. The task falsification is seriously eating data.

Actually, we are talking about Ego more now. In my opinion, Ego has proposed a better way to figure out. This is undeniable. But the problem now is whether the data taken only from the head camera can be used. If the salesperson really develops and we want to do some detailed movements of the hand, is there any help? These things are still unknown.

So the most important thing for GSM to solve now is data. It should be data that can be scaled and can be used by models. I think this can be used by models. The two things that can be used and can be scaled are a balance. Because the model wants the data to be better, the higher the quality, the more the model, the better. But if your needs are higher, I can't scale it, so it becomes a custom. How to balance quality and quantity? Which things in my model can be abandoned. This may not be clearly defined yet. Once this is clearly defined, I think the rest will be accelerated.

二十八、创业新感受

这是你第一次创业，有什么新感受？

For me, there are two firsts. The first startup contains two parts.

The first part is that I think the first face is down. This is the first time.

The second time is from a landing perspective, what I really understand is that we used to pay more attention to the priority of technology. Now we pay more attention to which aspect of technology has value. Is it just that technologists think there are many things that can be prioritized?

你现在优先什么？

I definitely want to have more tasks that can support me. I will prioritize the scene and the fun of the task. This is the first step — the business part.

Then let's talk about the creative part. I think the first step is to learn how to bet. The business must be bet. No one knows which route will be successful. And resources must be limited. So in the case of uncertain routes, you have to bet. If everyone knows which route is successful, why are you successful? If that route is successful, the big market will be successful. This is 100%. The place with more resources and more people will definitely succeed. But if you hesitate when you don't know the route, it's very likely that nothing will come out in the end.

你的大 bet 是什么？

Is it a big bet not to make a body? Yes, I think the first one is the sensor is a big bet. Then the second one is the original is a big bet. Because the original is very likely to do this thing. I found it didn't work out at the end. You trained for half a day, trained for a year, spent a lot of resources. Then the model just didn't work.

Maybe it's also because of the lack of resources. You can only do a 100 元 project, but you have to do a 200 元 project. There is not so much resources. These are all a risk point. But I think once it is done, the sense of accomplishment is still relatively high.

二十九、蚂蚁对灵波的期待

蚂蚁对你们的期待是什么？

Because now the Ant Group is also AI first. From this big strategy, we also want to break through the upper limit of intelligence. AI first only includes two parts: AI in the physical world and AI in the digital world. We may carry the mission of the group to break through the upper limit of artificial intelligence in the physical world. This is a common thing. And another one is that My Group is still a core company that uses digital services as a core service. And I think this is also on the extension line of the entire group.

管理上呢？

In fact, overall, it's still more in accordance with the way of the startup company. It's just that our management system may be more independent. Because the business is relatively independent. So it may be a little bit independent when it's managed. But the overall infrastructure is shared.

你的 bet 集团的反馈是？

I think it's still supportive. The group has been supportive since the last release and this release. They said why we don't do the main body. Actually, there will be some debate. But I think the group has full trust and respect for Linbo because we are closer to the industry itself. So, in this regard, we made some decisions. The group will definitely give some suggestions from its perspective, but in the end, the two sides will still reach a consensus after a few rounds of exchanges.

创业最好的预期和最差的预期？

My best prediction is that I really saw the robot enter the house. The robot running into the house is the model of Linbo. This is my best prediction.

The worst prediction is that it didn't work. I don't have any worse predictions. Maybe I made a mistake in the process of betting.

你是个赌徒吗？

I'm okay.

三十、模型进展与预期对照

模型进展是符合预期、低于预期还是超预期？

Actually, it's a little higher than the previous one. Because when we talk about the origin, we start from two big pieces. One is the vision — the one that we just said we can see more clearly. I think we have already… This part is that the origin pushed it forward one step. And then it's more clear that we also have the origin and we have moved forward one step. The original idea of the architecture, whether it's the loss of time or the reasoning efficiency, etc.

And then there's another one that's more sophisticated. I think the more sophisticated one is the next original idea — the data original idea. Because I think that after the data is better scaled, there will definitely be better breakthroughs in the format of the task.

So I think that from the point of view of "we can see more clearly, think more clearly, and do more precisely", we have just pushed the first two points forward with the concept of "original" after half a年。 I didn't expect it to come so soon. I hope the data origin can come earlier than I expected. I may be happier.

三十一、行业格局：大厂 vs. 创业

现在不同领域的玩家都想接入机器人大脑，你们的优势和最终的行业格局？

The pattern is — I think it's similar to the large-scale model. There may be large factories that do better, and there may also be two or three startup companies that do better.

你们属于哪种？

I think we may be closer to startups now. We are a very special company, we are a startup company that relies on the big market.

I think from the intelligence level, it should be like this. There should be one or two players in the big market, and there will be two or three players in the startup company. Then everyone can run their own ecosystem, which includes the ecosystem of data.

本体的生态场景的生态就可能每家的模型因为你有了生态之后, 你场景加本体可能就会给你 the data in that ecosystem, your model will slowly be divided into more suitable ecosystems. Of course, maybe everyone will eventually reach a universal ecosystem, that is, into the family. But before that, each model may have different characteristics. For example, some models may be suitable for delicate tasks, while others may be suitable for long-term tasks.

I think from the perspective of a startup company, I think we can solve the most core problem in a stage. The most core problem right now is that there is not enough intelligence. In other words, is it a wheel or a foot? Or what should its structure look like? It's not the core point yet. The core point is that the intelligence is not enough, and the core point is that the data is not enough. So how to make the data scale up is the key. And when you have the intelligence, you can start to make landing attempts.

三十二、发布后的市场反馈

But now, especially after the release, I feel that my condition is a little bit better. I will think about what I should do next. I will review it and think about it. For example, how to combine data with models. These aspects will be considered more.

市场反馈如何？

It should be okay so far. Especially in the technical community.

你现在的核心指标是什么？

音效, 因為那個他講話 — he is the same as me. He is also from the Northeast. I think it's a point that I heard him speak very closely.

Another point is that I think it can quickly catch a major contradiction from a chaotic chaos.

举个例子？

When I graduated from the Department of Transformation, he wanted to participate. Because in the Department of Transformation, people often ask how I did it. But at that time, he asked me a question related to the industry or how I should use this thing.

这是谁？ 这是我当时做的那套视频编辑。 The biggest pain of the last AI was that it was difficult to land, and there was no good scene.

现在有人问你怎么用这个模型？

Definitely. In fact, I think that the giant intelligence is not as easy to spread as the large-scale model or the domotai model. Because it is too far from everyone's life. I need a machine to know if this thing is good or not.

Now most of them are developed. That's what I understand. The latest entertainment scenes in the retail market are the fastest to be detected. So I said it's not so easy to spread. And if it's a developer, he'll definitely want you to tell him how to use this thing. Because after all, all of our releases this time are basically pre-training. Pre-training needs to be done, or it needs to be done after training. After training itself is a very difficult thing. Or in other words, it's not like you just take the data, and throw it in, and simply adjust the parameters, and that's it.

If the effect is bad — is it because the training is not good, or the data is not taken well, or the model is not good? How to diagnose the problem? How to solve it after diagnosis? I think it's a very difficult thing.

I think if you can make a mobile game that can interact with people in real-time, many people will be willing to play it.

三十三、快问快答

你在世界上最喜欢的食物？ Desserts.

你在世界上最喜欢的地方？ Home.

推荐一本书？ Life's book, The Wilderness of the Wilderness. I really like martial arts. I've been obsessed with financial novels since I was a kid. I really like it. I've actually read financial novels many times. But I recommend 笑傲江湖 every time. Because I think I especially like the more grand look of the Linguine. I don't care about anything. I really like that kind of psychological state.

你是这样的人吗？ I want to be such a person.

如果机器人有人格，你希望它是什么？ I want it to be a J person. He's easy to work with. Yes, I think its core is still to be used. I hope he is a "this person". In other words, if I have to choose between providing emotional value and working, I will definitely choose working.

为什么不提供情绪价值？ I think emotional value should be provided by people.

影响机器人进步的文章有哪些？ Actually, it may not necessarily be articles. For example, they don't write articles anymore, they write blogs. The Gen1 of Generalist should have a big impact on us. It's really good at scaling up its data. And then, the work of Pi is also very good. And then, the work of Google DeepMind is also very good.

三十四、中国本土优势

在中国不用本地硬件优势会可惜。

Yes, I think it will be a pity. But the hardware advantage may have an indelible effect in the development of this robot. The robot still says that no matter what kind of digital method you use, you must rely on hardware and sensors.

I think from the data quality, I always said that I think it's a transformation of Internet popularity. Or the data is accumulated from the Internet era. But compared to the Internet, I think it may be — especially the data of G-SEN — may be an empty window period. Now everyone is the same. So it may have an advantage in terms of data collection.

So we actually have a lot of this. We have our own so-called data alliance. We will have some better data partners. Then maybe we will talk to them and see how to do this data better together. Because all the data you have to have standards. So in this regard, we are actively trying to take advantage of this industry.

结束语

Alright, that's it for today's program. This is Business Interviews, a deep-dive interview program produced by the Language and World Studio. You can go to the public account to follow our studio and get more information. Our public account is Language and World. Language is World. We hope to explore a new world with you from here. You are also welcome to interact with us in the comments section of Little Universe.

## 一、最反直觉的观察：中国机器人生态正在"角色互换"
过去十年的产业刻板印象是——美国团队做大脑，中国团队做本体。但 2026 年出现的这波"从本体转向大脑"的浪潮，实际上是**中国硬件太成熟带来的反噬**。当灵巧手从"稀缺"走向"即将标准化"，当传感器从算力受限走向富余，整条硬件价值链正在快速下沉为"大宗商品"。价值必然向上游迁移——这不是因为大家突然爱上了大脑，而是**硬件红利到期后的资本自然选择**。沈宇军讲的"下一代硬件会由智能重新定义"其实是同一句话的镜像表达：现在做本体的人在为下一代模型公司提供**过渡形态**。
一个更有意思的镜像：美国 PI 押注 zero-shot（尽量不做后训练），而中国的灵波、Generalist 强调"高效后训练"——这看似技术路线之争，深层其实是**基础设施可用性差异**塑造出来的哲学：数据丰沛地区可以赌通用，数据稀缺地区不得不押可迁移性。技术路线在多大程度上是环境的映射，比研究者自己愿意承认的要多得多。

沈宇军举的那个例子——数字世界的 DINO 能穿透玻璃"看见"猫，但物理世界必须

item.title: [Dwarkesh Clips] You Could Be Inside a Black Hole Right Now – Adam Brown
item.dc:creator: Dwarkesh Clips
item.content:encoded:
💡 创造性洞见

一、最令人震撼的悖论：你可能"注定死亡"却毫不知情

Adam Brown 揭示了一个几乎违反直觉的事实：事件视界不是一个"地方"，而是一个"命运宣告"。它没有物理标志、没有围栏、没有闪光——它是一个目的论事实（teleological fact），只有从"未来"回望才能被定义。

这里藏着一个极其反常识的洞察：在足够大的黑洞里，你可以出生、恋爱、生儿育女、写完一部小说、看着孙辈长大——全程都在"已死"状态中。"doomed but not dead"（注定死亡但尚未死去）这个区分，可能是物理学中最接近哲学的表述之一。它把"死亡"这个二元事件，撕裂成了两个不同的时间坐标。

二、意想不到的跨领域连接：事件视界 = 沉没成本 = 组织路径依赖

事件视界的数学结构，与人类决策系统中的"不可逆临界点"惊人同构： - 一段婚姻、一份职业、一家公司的战略转向——外部观察者往往比当事人更早看到"视界"已被跨越（时间膨胀的隐喻：局内人感觉"一切如常，一秒一秒过"，局外人却看到他们的"信号红移到消失"）。 - 硅谷投资人常说"公司在死之前 18 个月就已经死了"——这就是一个组织学的事件视界。CEO 内部体验一切正常，董事会外部却已经看不见他们的信号。

更妙的是：黑洞越大，跨越视界越无痛。这精确对应了大型组织的悲剧——规模越大的系统，从"注定失败"到"实际崩溃"之间的距离越长，当事人越难察觉。柯达、诺基亚在跨越自己的"事件视界"那一刻，内部体验的潮汐力几乎为零。

三、隐藏的系统性真相：观察者视角的分裂就是"现实"本身

大多数人以为相对论说的是"时间是相对的"，但 Brown 描述的场景暗示了一个更深的命题：两个都"正确"的观察者，会构建出根本不相容的因果叙事——一个人说"你从未跨越视界，只是慢慢褪成黑色"，另一个人说"我平静地穿过去了，还活了一辈子"。两者都对，两者都完整，两者不可调和。

这不是物理学的怪癖，而是所有复杂系统的通用属性： - 患者和医生看同一次诊断 - 员工和管理层看同一次裁员 - 用户和产品经理看同一次改版

我们习惯性地问"到底发生了什么？"——但黑洞告诉我们，这个问题根本没有唯一答案。真相是一个由观察者位置定义的场。

最刺骨的启发：你此刻可能正生活在某个"社会性黑洞"内部——一段关系、一个信念系统、一种生活方式——从内部感知一切如常（1 秒/秒），而从外部看，你早已"红移到不可见"。你无法通过局部测量发现自己是否跨越了视界。唯一的诊断工具是找到一个"远处的观察者"，看看他们是否还能收到你的光。

📝 转录文本

提问：掉入黑洞会看到什么？

Dwarkesh： So suppose, um, one learns all these equations, but then finds himself in the unfortunate position of falling into a black hole. What would they see?

Adam Brown： Great question. So, there's actually two different perspectives you could take. One is the perspective for me watching you falling into the black hole. The other is the perspective of you falling into the black hole. And those two perspectives are consistent with each other, but interestingly different. So, maybe I should describe them both.

视角一：外部观察者眼中的坠落

So, first let's ask the question, what do I see as you fall into the black hole? What I see, this is of course how fast you need to how hard you need to fire your rocket to as not fall into the black hole, but you're not going to do this. You're just going to sit here a long, long way away from the black hole. You're going to turn off your rocket and accept what comes.

And what comes is you'll slowly accelerate towards the black hole with a rate first given by the Newtonian formula, and then when you get close to the black hole, start picking up corrections — start picking up general relativity corrections to the Newtonian inverse square law.

Um, and so what I will see as I watch you fall towards the black hole is first, you'll go faster and faster and faster towards the black hole as you fall down the gravitational potential of the black hole. Uh, and faster and faster and faster, but then something strange will happen, which is you'll stop going faster and you'll start going slower.

引力时间膨胀与红移

And the reason you're going slower is that as I watch you, you start to get gravitational time dilation as you fall down here, and I see start to see you running slow, your clock running slow. This is the formula for if you were static. You're not static, you're moving. So, there's a some other formula, but the formula has the same effect, which is that as you get closer and closer towards the black hole, your wristwatch starts running slower and slower and slower.

And in fact, if you do the appropriate integral, I never see you cross the event horizon. I just see you getting closer and closer to the event horizon, but slowing and slowing and slowing as you get closer and closer to the event horizon.

Uh, and as I watch you, I'm presumably using light to watch you, that light gets more and more red-shifted. The wavelength gets longer and longer. Uh the longer the wavelength of light, the harder it is even to really see you. I start getting — you start getting delocalized by the wavelength of the light. And eventually I just stop seeing you entirely. There's a final photon that I see that you emit, and then you just fade to black, fade through red to black. I never see you cross the event horizon.

Uh this was noticed by people in the early days of general relativity and greatly confused them. And they started to think that something you would experience something funny yourself as you fell across the event horizon. That is that is not true.

视角二：坠落者自身的体验

In fact, if I instead adopt the perspective of you, from your point of view, your clock isn't running slow, it's running at 1 second per second. If you look back at me, there's some funny stuff going on to do with me me running fast perhaps, but as far as you're concerned, everything's totally normal. You accelerate towards the black hole. You're getting faster and faster and faster as you approach the black hole. And you just sail across the event horizon totally as as normal.

潮汐力：取决于黑洞的大小

The event horizon is not a particularly violent place for you. You can calculate the tidal forces um as you cross the event horizon, or as you approach and then across the event horizon, and they're not particularly big. Uh or rather for large black holes, they're not particularly big.

For a solar mass black hole, they would be pretty big and would be pretty painful for you. You'd find that your feet are being attracted to the black hole much more vigorously than your head is cuz they're closer, uh and you end up getting stretched.

But if I take a big enough black hole, uh you wouldn't notice anything funny happening whatsoever. Um the bigger the black hole, the smaller the tidal effects. And if I took a black hole the mass of the galaxy, uh you'd be basically fine as you cross the event horizon. If I took an even bigger black hole than that, uh you could live out your entire life uh having crossed the event horizon of the black hole um before you hit the singularity, which is fatal.

"注定死亡，但尚未死去"

Um, when you cross the event horizon, uh, you are doomed. You are doomed because, uh, once you cross the event horizon, you must proceed to the singularity. There's no way you can fire a rocket to stop yourself hitting the singularity. You are doomed, but you are not dead. Uh, you are only for sure dead once you hit the singularity and get spaghettified, get mangled by the tidal forces.

But, for a large enough black hole, uh, you can be doomed and not even know it. Uh, the event horizon is really a not locally measurable quantity. It is a teleological fact. It says that once you have crossed the event horizon, you must proceed to the singularity, but it can take a long time to get there for a large enough black hole.

Uh, you could in principle, for a large enough black hole, uh, live out uh, your entire life if you had a black hole that was, you know, many light centuries across. Uh, you could live out your life, you could have descendants, all of whom live inside the black hole, and only once you really approach the singularity, do the tidal forces get strong and kill you.

If you enjoyed this clip, you can watch the full episode here and subscribe for more clips. Thanks.

## 一、最令人震撼的悖论：你可能"注定死亡"却毫不知情
Adam Brown 揭示了一个几乎违反直觉的事实：**事件视界不是一个"地方"，而是一个"命运宣告"**。它没有物理标志、没有围栏、没有闪光——它是一个**目的论事实（teleological fact）**，只有从"未来"回望才能被定义。
这里藏着一个极其反常识的洞察：**在足够大的黑洞里，你可以出生、恋爱、生儿育女、写完一部小说、看着孙辈长大——全程都在"已死"状态中**。"doomed but not dead"（注定死亡但尚未死去）这个区分，可能是物理学中最接近哲学的表述之一。它把"死亡"这个二元事件，撕裂成了两个不同的时间坐标。
## 二、意想不到的跨领域连接：事件视界 = 沉没成本 = 组织路径依赖
**事件视界的数学结构，与人类决策系统中的"不可逆临界点"惊人同构**： - 一段婚姻、一份职业、一家公司的战略转向——**外部观察者往往比当事人更早看到"视界"已被跨越**（时间膨胀的隐喻：局内人感觉"一切如常，一秒一秒过"，局外人却看到他们的"信号红移到消失"）。 - 硅谷投资人常说"公司在死之前 18 个

item.title: [Bits + Bips] Stripe Bid $53B for PayPal: Who Actually Wins Stablecoin Payments?
item.dc:creator: Bits + Bips
item.content:encoded:
💡 创造性洞见

一、被忽视的"反向估值套利"：私募泡沫正在吞噬公开市场的现金牛

表面上，Stripe 竞购 PayPal 是一场支付巨头的整合戏码。但真正令人意外的是——这是一次估值体系的"反向殖民"。历史上，公开市场公司用自己流动的股票去收购非流动的私营公司，因为公开股票被视为"硬通货"。现在情况倒转了：VC 为了避免 mark-to-market 而人为维持 Stripe 的高估值，让它反过来用"私募软通货"去吞噬公开市场那些自由现金流收益率高达 11% 的真实业务。

这里藏着一个跨领域的诡异连接：这与 2000 年代初期次贷 CDO 的运作机制在结构上惊人相似——把不透明、难以定价的资产（私募估值/次级贷款）打包，用其"信用等级"（虚高估值/AAA 评级）去撬动真实的现金流资产。当一个市场的定价机制脱离流动性检验时，它就会开始外溢并扭曲其他市场。 你以为你在看支付行业新闻，其实你在看私募/公募估值套利周期的顶部信号之一。

二、PayPal 的失败不是执行问题，而是"报纸互联网化"的经典陷阱——但这个陷阱在稳定币领域有个更深层的隐喻

Austin 说 PayPal "选择了失败"。这个说法背后其实揭示了一个组织行为学的深层规律：当一家公司拥有巨大的存量用户基础时，它对新技术的最优策略在数学上就是"最小化摧毁自身现金流"，而不是"最大化利用新技术"。这就是为什么 PYUSD 在美国境内、小额、非机构可用——这些恰恰是 PayPal 现有业务最不受威胁的领域。

跨领域连接：这与生物学中的"内共生理论"形成鲜明对比。当古细菌吞噬了线粒体前身时，它没有把线粒体当成"细菌版的自己"来使用，而是让线粒体完全按自己的能量代谢方式运作——结果诞生了真核生物。PayPal 把区块链当成"数字化的 PayPal ledger"来用，Robinhood 通过 USDG 却是把自己的用户基础当作"稳定币的宿主"，让稳定币按自己的逻辑运作。前者是消化，后者是共生。这就是为什么 Robinhood 可能真正会成功——它不是"把 Robinhood 放到链上"，而是"把用户放进稳定币经济"。

三、真正意料之外的洞察：AI 开源模型正在触发一场"监管套利大迁徙"，而它的镜像早就在加密领域上演过

Kimi K3 的发布看似是中美 AI 竞争的又一回合，但真正值得注意的是 David Sachs 引用的那个细节：美国研究人员因为 guardrail 无法用美国模型分析真实的漏洞样本，被迫切换到本地运行的中国 GLM 模型。这不是简单的"中国追赶美国"，这是监管溢价正在把最有价值的用例推向开源和境外。

跨领域连接（这才是真正的惊喜）：这与 2017-2020 年 ICO 时代的资本外流几乎是同一部剧本。当美国 SEC 对 ICO 采取"执法即监管"时，项目方、开发者和资本大规模迁移到新加坡、瑞士、开曼。基础设施创新会寻找监管阻力最小的路径流动，无论那是资本、代码还是模型权重。

更深层的模式是：当一项技术的能力增长速度快过监管适应速度时，"合规溢价"就会翻转为"合规折价"。这是节目里所有话题——Stripe/PayPal、稳定币标准之争、Clarity Act 的博弈、Kimi K3 的开源——背后同一个隐藏结构。它们都是同一个物理规律的不同侧面：在信息与资本高流动性的世界里，"守门人"的稀缺租金正在被系统性地套利掉。

一个让人后背发凉的推论：如果这个规律成立，那么真正会在未来十年跑赢的资产，不是那些依赖监管护城河的中间商（Circle、大银行、传统持牌机构），而是那些能把"合规成本"内化为产品优势的分发型公司（Stripe、Robinhood、可能还有 JPMorgan 的稳定币）。护城河不再是牌照本身，而是同时能满足合规与用户体验的极窄通道。

📝 转录文本

Stripe Bid $53B for PayPal: Who Actually Wins Stablecoin Payments?

开场：Oracle 与 AI 敞口的意外脆弱性

There's a cloud business directly indexed to OpenAI. It's called Oracle. Oracle's got a big contract backlog where they face off with OpenAI and their stock price dropped 4% today. It's plumbing new lows as we speak, down 50% in the year. So it's not going to lower demand for semiconductors. We still need semiconductors, but it is creating credit risk if you face off with OpenAI who signed up a trillion dollars in these revenue obligations. That's why Oracle is feeling the pain here.

There was a bit of an own goal here — the founder of that company is a Carnegie Mellon University graduate. So, you know, we lost this amazing talent to a geopolitical competitor, which is unfortunate.

节目介绍与市场快照

Hey everyone, welcome to Bits and Bips, where we explore how crypto and macro collide one basis point at a time. We're here to discuss the latest stories in the worlds of crypto and macro.

As a quick market snapshot of the day: - Bitcoin's around 65K as I'm reading this - ETH around 1890 - SOL around 77.5 - HYPE is back to 62 - WTI is at 83, Brent's at 89 - SpaceX at 120 - Circle at 65.5

However, before we begin, a quick commercial break.
